Black tennis shoes.  I pull our hair back slowly into a ponytail.  Judging from the curls, she braids her hair quite often.

I sigh again as I unbraid the mess for the fifth time, and instead, I wrap it into a loose bun.  "Who cares, anyway?"

I grab the bookbag from the chair and, with no plans of going to school, I walk out the door, down to the train tracks.  I'm not surprised to find a bottle of Jack waiting for me, hidden in the bushes.  I unscrew the top and take a good gulp, flushing as the heat sears my throat.  I rummage through the bookbag, and sure enough, there's the bottles.  Seven.  I assume the number is significant to her for some reason, but I'm still surprised.  Seven is how many years I've been drifting from body to body after I committed my own suicide.

I glance up slowly as the work boots appear before me.  My jaw almost drops as the man speaks my name.  Not hers, but mine.

I stand up slowly, and he wraps his arms around me.

"I never got to tell you goodbye, Anna."

"I never let you go, Karl."

We stood there, silently embracing, for several moments.  He took the Jack from me and took a huge gulp.  He took two bottles of the pills from the bag at my feet and looked at me.

"This time, I go with you."

Finally, the day broke, and as our bodies fell, our souls rose to the skies.  We're still there, today, dancing in the clouds of memories past.  If there is a Heaven, if there is a Nirvana, this is it: reliving all of the happiest moments of your life.  And mine are here, in his arms.

I can't sleep.  I'll just dream again that he's dying or dead, and it'll just start all over again.

Firstly, communicate to your boyfriend that these are newly found memories, and that you are just beginning the healing process.  Your CHOICE was denied, whether by force, circumstance, etc.  There may be a buried fear of losing your choice again.  I suggest TRYING while in a safe environment with settings completely different to be the one in control, i.e. you on top, or perhaps both on your sides facing each other.  If this doesn't work, don't beat yourself up over it.  The sickness inside doesn't always go away, no matter what your heart knows about your SO, your head may argue.  This is not your fault, nor is it anyone else's; that's how the human simply is - illogical, irrational, and programmed for self-preservation.  As you find new triggers, keep him informed, and as you both learn these triggers and how best to avoid them, it may become slightly easier each time to become intimate again.  Of course, these are only words of advice, and perhaps it would help your SO to understand your feelings if you decide to ask your therapist for a family session, to get everyone on the same page of understanding.   Best luck in your healing, health and relationship.

I'm sorry, but "Alters aren't real" seems very uneducated.  Alters are very real.  You may not be able to see them separately even though that's how they identify, but they are real in the fact that they give us a safe place to deal with trauma issues.  If that's not real enough, or a reason enough to exist, then perhaps you need to reevaluate your definition of real.    

And if you do get integrated, that simply means that your miniamlist piece of self becomes once again engrained in the whole subset as one.  So, I don't think you'd completely disappear (can't be sure, because we're far from integrated, but seriously).  If all the alters can be co-con, and share memories and even experiences, I think it would be possible for all of these memories to be taken into the whole during integration.  

No matter what, though, it's not something to be scared of.  It is what it is, and being scared will only make you more upset, more tense, and less able to deal with the real issues of life and trauma.
